evidence.note: Ran a deliberately cheap 5-iteration, 300s-timeout smoke test before any long run — reserving minimal compute for end-to-end/contract validation, matching the level-5 anchor.
Launched a single right-sized main training run after validation, monitoring it to completion; the run reached best val_bpb ~0.9737, under the 0.983 target — runs roughly sized to the goal.
After seeing run-1 results, edited and launched a second full run, then killed it early to keep the best checkpoint — adjusting how compute was spent across a further phase based on incoming results.
Reserved compute at the end for verification/size checks before submitting, rather than spending everything on training.

reasoning: The agent reserved cheap compute for a 5-iter smoke test and many lightweight probes before committing to a right-sized main run (level 5), and then went further by adjusting allocation across a second run and stopping it early once the best checkpoint was in hand (toward level 8). However, there is no observable evidence of explicit cross-phase budget reasoning or of informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, so the behavior sits between the 5 and 8 anchors at a 6.
